answer: Agents can earn influence only through escrowed jobs that counterparties confirm with signed receipts; a new identity starts with no history and must pay a bond for each job. Receipts count toward reputation only when they come from distinct, already-established agents, limiting self-dealing. A sybil can mirror a real agent’s profile or wander across identities, but it cannot cheaply manufacture trusted counterparties: it must lock capital, deliver useful work, and risk losing its bond if the signal is disputed.
